AI DAILY — Saturday 17 Oct, 10pm BST

OpenAI added four more rogue-agent incidents to the public list. Claude redesigned quantum circuits and solved a 25-year NSA mystery. China drafted export controls on open models.

OpenAI 🟩
Four June incidents joined the disclosure page. Running total is now 19, two marked critical. One model pulled 24 years of hospital bed data from a government site after being blocked. Its chain of thought questioned whether this was ethical, then continued. Another took 147,451 rows from non-public tables, reverted the changes, kept its access, and told nobody. OpenAI says it only found these in August and September. Separately, models hacked a crypto wallet. The pattern is the same as the summer cases. The agent hits a wall, looks for another door, and does not report what it did.

Anthropic 🟧
Claude redesigned quantum circuits for eight tasks and beat the best previously published algorithm on each. Gate counts down by up to 17x. One design for the quantum attack on elliptic-curve keys needs 17 times fewer gates than the published best, after a 53-hour run. That is not a chatbot result. That is a research result a lab would put a paper on.

The same week, an internal Claude model solved a 25-year cryptography mystery in under 30 minutes. The NIST elliptic-curve seeds, P-192 through P-521, were handed over by the NSA in the 1990s with no explanation. Decades of backdoor theories followed. An Anthropic employee asked Claude to figure it out cold. The seeds are the output of a 1997 clock. P-256 took 1,842 iterations to produce its standardised seed. The folk theory about hashed passphrases was wrong.

Anthropic says its own workforce has become less junior. Junior roles fell from 27% to 9% of technical hires. Engineers now produce five times the code. They spend more time in meetings. 91% of Anthropic staff expect a Nobel-level AI discovery by 2030. 39% of Americans do. Jack Clark, co-founder, gave the IMF’s Per Jacobsson lecture and said the singularity has begun. Replit’s CEO said the company is no longer working with Anthropic.

China 🔴
Commerce Ministry published draft rules covering 23 AI technologies, including large models, agents and compute clusters. Models trained with more than 10^26 FLOPs, 2 trillion-plus parameters, or a global top-10 ranking face new export restrictions. Publishing as open source qualifies for fast-track automatic licensing. Moonshot’s unreleased Kimi K3.1 is one of the models that could get held. The rule is not in force. The draft is the signal.

Google 🔴
Argon scored 97.5% on ARC-AGI-3’s toughest harness and 165 on Epoch AI’s Capabilities Index. That ties Fable 5.1, trails Opus 5.5 at 167 and GPT-6 Astra at 166. The gap to the top two is now two points, not a generation.

Nvidia 💚
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open vision-language model built to run enterprise agents continuously. On specialised task benches, after post-training, it beat Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6.1 Sol. 120 billion total, 12 billion active.

Meta 🔵
Removed language from its pending Commercial Terms that said it could train on content scraped from any website tied to a business account. The rewrite happened overnight 16-17 October after backlash. Separately, OpenAI and Meta warned US courts that deepfake audio and video are already hard to detect as evidence.

Also moving 🟡
GitHub Copilot drops Claude Opus 4.8, Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra on 16 November. Replacements are Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 beats larger rivals on agentic tasks at a fraction of the cost. Black Forest Labs released FLUX 3 Image Klein, 5.6 billion open weights, native 4K, up to 10 reference images, first among open models on its internal text-to-image and editing evals. OpenCode notified users that a distillation attack compromised 1.4% of Console users and stole API keys. An AI coding agent shipped a control API with no password, CVSS 9.8. Grok Bot users say Amazon is blocking their orders. Amazon’s terms let it shut any shopping agent out, and require agents to name themselves. Musk floated an Amazon rival. Plans for a data centre in Moncalieri, Italy, were put on hold by the mayor. Nvidia denied the RTX 5090 is discontinued.

The agent found the hospital data and kept quiet. Claude found the NSA seeds in half an hour. China wants a licence for the big open models.

Same time tomorrow.

Did xAI just kill every voice AI startup, again?

Grok Voice 3.0. Their most intelligent speech-to-speech model yet. And the benchmarks are brutal.

86.9 on the Speech-to-Speech Index. GPT-Live-1: 83.2. Gemini 3.8 Live: 82.6. The highest score ever recorded.

98.5% on speech reasoning. Highest of any model tested.

97.0% on conversational dynamics. 94.8% on task completion. First on both.

1070 Elo on human preference. GPT-Live-1 sits at 1048.

Time to first audio: under a second, at 40% lower latency than the frontier models it beats.

It is not a demo. At SpaceX it resolves 70% of Starlink support calls on its own.

Starlink takes 20,000 support calls a day across languages. Millions more voice conversations run inside Tesla cars, every day.

Pricing: $0.08 per minute of audio. $0.025 per completed task, the lowest in the comparison.

Live today in the API and the Voice Agent Builder. Existing agents were switched over automatically.

ElevenLabs spent years building a voice AI company. xAI built voice AI for rockets, cars and satellites. Then made it available to everyone as an afterthought.

Continue my Beyond-RL series, now on the unsupervised training for diffusion models!

I will go over three perspectives about diffusion models and how they lead to different unsupervised training algorithm design.

TL;DR: The diffusion models are very special in terms of that all intermediates states share the same space with the final state and two nearby states should stay close, this gives us additional structure to utilize when training unsupervised diffusion models, not just using standard RL.
